entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv4289"/><div sID="gen6216" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv4289"/><hi type="bold">2-4. Shechaniah ... answered and said unto Ezra, We have trespassed--</hi>This was one of the leading men, who was not himself a delinquent in the matter, for his name does not occur in the following list. He spoke in the general name of the people, and his conduct evinced a tender conscience, as well as no small fortitude in making such a proposal; for as his father and five paternal uncles (<reference osisRef="Ezra.10.26">Ezr 10:26</reference>) were involved in the guilt of unlawful marriages, he showed, by the measure he recommended, that he deemed it better to obey God than to please his nearest relatives.<div eID="gen6216" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen6217" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">yet now there is hope in Israel concerning this thing--</hi>This hope, however, depended on timely measures of reformation, and therefore, instead of surrendering themselves to despair or despondency, he counselled them to amend their error without delay, relying on God's mercy for the past. Though the proposal may seem harsh and cruel, yet in the peculiar circumstances of the Jews it was just as well as necessary; and he urged the duty of seeing it executed on Ezra, as the only person competent to carry it into effect, being possessed of skill and address for so delicate and difficult a work, and invested by God, and under Him by the Persian king (<reference osisRef="Ezra.7.23-Ezra.7.28">Ezr 7:23-28</reference>), with the requisite authority to enforce it. <div eID="gen6217" type="x-p"/>
